## Mitigation Checklist

When designing systems with external input or cross-process interactions, apply these four core mitigations:

### 1. Principle of Least Privilege
Grant write scope only to the paths a process genuinely needs. Do not hand a subprocess or external library permission to write everywhere; restrict it to exactly what is required for its function.

### 2. Input Validation at Trust Boundaries
Treat all external content as untrusted data, never as instructions. Validate, parse, and sanitize input at every boundary where untrusted data enters a trusted component. Do not allow a source to reshape your own logic.

### 3. Path Canonicalization
Resolve and validate file paths before any write to block directory traversal and other path-manipulation attacks. Normalize paths to their canonical form and check they remain within allowed bounds.

### 4. Audit Logging
Record every denied action with its reason for later review. Logging creates accountability and makes it possible to detect attacks after they occur. Do not silently fail — log the event and the reason it was rejected.
